//: Hand-written starter questions (ADR 0010). Imported at start-up by key; edits made in /admin are kept. Little picture questions are live with word cards until they have pictures (2026-11-26). Facts were checked on 2026-11-26.

questions.prompt: Which animal says moo?
questions.explain: Cows say moo. I say moo when I'm sad. Different reasons.

questions.prompt: Which animal says quack?
questions.explain: Ducks quack. They also bite. Ask me how I know.

questions.prompt: What color is a banana?
questions.explain: Yellow! Unless you leave it on the counter for a week. Then it's brown and sad.

questions.prompt: Which one can fly?
questions.explain: Birds fly. Fish swim. Dogs nap. I relate to the dog.

questions.prompt: Which shape is round?
questions.explain: A circle! Round and round and round. Like this game.

questions.prompt: Which animal lives in the water?
questions.explain: Fish live in the water. So did I, back when I had a ship.

questions.prompt: Which one is hot?
questions.explain: The sun is super hot. Don't touch it. Seriously.

questions.prompt: Which one is a fruit?
questions.explain: An apple! Please don't eat the shoe.

questions.prompt: How many days are in a week?
questions.explain: Seven. Five of them are Monday, emotionally.

questions.prompt: What do bees make?
questions.explain: Honey! Bees work all summer for it, then we steal it. Pirate move, honestly.

questions.prompt: Which planet do we live on?
questions.explain: Earth. Last I checked. I'll check again later.

questions.prompt: What is the biggest animal that has ever lived?
questions.explain: The blue whale. Bigger than any dinosaur. Its heart is the size of a small car.

questions.prompt: What color do you get when you mix blue and yellow?
questions.explain: Green! Like my face after I lose. Which is every round.

questions.prompt: How many legs does a spider have?
questions.explain: Eight. Eight legs. All of them running toward me.

questions.prompt: True or false: a tomato is a fruit.
questions.explain: True! It grows from a flower and has seeds. Ketchup is basically jam. Fight me.

questions.prompt: What does a caterpillar turn into?
questions.explain: A butterfly! It goes into a cocoon a little worm and comes out fancy. Inspiring.

questions.prompt: How many points does a snowflake usually have?
questions.explain: Six, because of the way water freezes. No two exactly alike. Like my excuses.

questions.prompt: What is the largest ocean on Earth?
questions.explain: The Pacific. I sailed it once. Well, a bit of it. The bit near the dock.

questions.prompt: What is the capital of France?
questions.explain: Paris. I'm banned from two of its cafés.

questions.prompt: How many continents are there?
questions.explain: Seven, the way most schools count them. Some countries count six. Nobody counts eight. Nobody.

questions.prompt: Which planet is called the Red Planet?
questions.explain: Mars. It's red because of rusty dust. Same as my old ship.

questions.prompt: Which gas do plants take in from the air to make food?
questions.explain: Carbon dioxide. They breathe in what we breathe out. Teamwork.

questions.prompt: Who painted the Mona Lisa?
questions.explain: Leonardo da Vinci. Took him years. I can't finish a sandwich.

questions.prompt: What is the hardest natural material?
questions.explain: Diamond. Second hardest: this question, apparently.

questions.prompt: How many sides does a hexagon have?
questions.explain: Six. Bees build with them. Bees are smarter than me.

questions.prompt: What is the tallest mountain above sea level?
questions.explain: Everest, about 8,849 meters. I get winded on stairs.

questions.prompt: Before pumpkins, what did people in Ireland carve for Halloween?
questions.explain: Turnips! Smaller, harder and much creepier. Pumpkins were a big upgrade.

questions.prompt: What is the chemical symbol for gold?
questions.explain: Au, from the Latin aurum. Ag is silver. I had both once. Briefly.

questions.prompt: In which year did people first walk on the Moon?
questions.explain: 1969, Apollo 11. They had less computing power than your phone. Your phone uses it for this.

questions.prompt: Which part of a cell is called its powerhouse?
questions.explain: The mitochondria. The one fact everyone remembers from biology.

questions.prompt: What is the smallest prime number?
questions.explain: Two. The only even prime. One doesn't count. One never counts.

questions.prompt: Which country has the most people?
questions.explain: India. It passed China around 2023, by the UN's count.

questions.prompt: Which animal has fingerprints so like ours that they could confuse a crime scene?
questions.explain: The koala! Even under a microscope they're hard to tell apart. Koalas: suspects.

questions.prompt: Which element has the atomic number 1?
questions.explain: Hydrogen. Simplest atom there is. Relatable.

questions.prompt: What is the longest river in Africa?
questions.explain: The Nile. Some say longest in the world; the Amazon fans disagree. Loudly.

questions.prompt: How many bones are in an adult human body?
questions.explain: 206. Babies have more; some fuse as you grow. Mine mostly ache.

questions.prompt: What is the tallest building in the world?
questions.explain: The Burj Khalifa in Dubai, about 828 meters. For now: Jeddah Tower is being built to beat it.

questions.prompt: True or false: lightning never strikes the same place twice.
questions.explain: False. The Empire State Building gets hit about 20 times a year. Lightning holds grudges.

questions.prompt: Besides lime, what is the main ingredient in a classic margarita?
questions.explain: Tequila. Ask me how many I've had tonight. Actually, don't.

questions.prompt: Which animal says woof?
questions.explain: Woof woof! Dogs are the best. Don't tell the cat.

questions.prompt: Which animal says meow?
questions.explain: Meow! Cats say that when they want snacks. So, always.

questions.prompt: What do you wear on your feet?
questions.explain: Shoes! A hat on your feet would be very silly. I tried it.

questions.prompt: What color is the sky on a sunny day?
questions.explain: Blue! Unless you're inside. Then it's ceiling colored.

questions.prompt: What color is grass?
questions.explain: Green! Grass is green. My face is green after boat rides.

questions.prompt: Which animal is the biggest?
questions.explain: The elephant! Elephants are huge. Mice are teeny.

questions.prompt: What do we brush our teeth with?
questions.explain: A toothbrush! Brush, brush, brush. Sparkly teeth!

questions.prompt: How many legs does a bird have?
questions.explain: Two! Birds stand on two skinny legs. Wobbly.

questions.prompt: Which one is cold?
questions.explain: Ice is cold! Brrr. Don't put it down my shirt.

questions.prompt: Which one can you ride?
questions.explain: A bike! Don't ride the banana. It ends badly.

questions.prompt: What do we use to see?
questions.explain: Eyes! You see with your eyes and smell with your nose. I smell like the sea.

questions.prompt: Which shape has three sides?
questions.explain: A triangle! One, two, three sides. Pointy!

questions.prompt: How many wheels does a bicycle have?
questions.explain: Two. Three is a tricycle. One is a unicycle, and a circus.

questions.prompt: What is frozen water called?
questions.explain: Ice! Heat it up and it's water again. Heat that up and it's steam.

questions.prompt: Which planet is closest to the Sun?
questions.explain: Mercury, the tiny speedy one. Toasty.

questions.prompt: How many months are in a year?
questions.explain: Twelve. Fifty-two is weeks. Nice try though.

questions.prompt: What do you call a baby dog?
questions.explain: A puppy! A kitten is a baby cat. A cub is a baby bear. Adorable, all of them.

questions.prompt: Which of these is a mammal?
questions.explain: Dolphins are mammals. They breathe air, like us. Well, like you. I mostly sigh.

questions.prompt: What shape is a stop sign?
questions.explain: An octagon: eight sides. Stop and count them sometime.

questions.prompt: What is 5 + 7?
questions.explain: Twelve. Count it on your fingers and toes if you need to.

questions.prompt: Which animal is called the king of the jungle?
questions.explain: The lion. Funny thing: lions mostly live on grassy plains, not in jungles.

questions.prompt: What do plants need from the sun to grow?
questions.explain: Light! Plants turn sunlight into food. I turn sunlight into a sunburn.

questions.prompt: In which sport do you score a touchdown?
questions.explain: American football. Six points and a silly dance.

questions.prompt: Which instrument has black and white keys?
questions.explain: The piano. Eighty-eight keys. I can play one of them.

questions.prompt: What is the opposite of hot?
questions.explain: Cold! Opposites: hot and cold, up and down, me and good at trivia.

questions.prompt: What is the biggest planet in our solar system?
questions.explain: Jupiter. More than a thousand Earths could fit inside it.

questions.prompt: Which planet is famous for its rings?
questions.explain: Saturn! Its rings are made of ice and rock. Very fancy.

questions.prompt: Which part of your body pumps blood?
questions.explain: Your heart. It beats about 100,000 times a day. Mine skips a few during these.

questions.prompt: Which gas do we need to breathe to stay alive?
questions.explain: Oxygen. Helium just makes you talk funny.

questions.prompt: What is the main ingredient in guacamole?
questions.explain: Avocado. Mashed, salted, gone in four minutes.

questions.prompt: How many strings does a standard guitar have?
questions.explain: Six. A bass usually has four. I have none. I sold it.

questions.prompt: Which is the largest country by area?
questions.explain: Russia, by a lot. It covers eleven time zones.

questions.prompt: At what temperature does water freeze in degrees Fahrenheit?
questions.explain: 32 degrees Fahrenheit. That's zero in Celsius. Science can't agree on anything.

questions.prompt: What do you call a word that means the same as another word?
questions.explain: A synonym. Like big and large. Or clever and me. No? Okay.

questions.prompt: Which famous ship sank in 1912 after hitting an iceberg?
questions.explain: The Titanic, on its very first trip. And people say I'm a bad captain.

questions.prompt: What is 9 × 8?
questions.explain: 72. Times tables: the ancient sea shanty of math.

questions.prompt: What is the capital of Japan?
questions.explain: Tokyo, one of the biggest cities on Earth.

questions.prompt: How many sides does a pentagon have?
questions.explain: Five. Penta means five. Octo means eight. Salty means zero right answers.

questions.prompt: What do bees collect from flowers to make honey?
questions.explain: Nectar, a sugary juice. Bees carry pollen around while they're at it.

questions.prompt: Which video game plumber wears a red cap?
questions.explain: Mario. Luigi wears green and gets far less credit. Sound familiar?

questions.prompt: How many players from each team are on a basketball court at once?
questions.explain: Five per team. Ten on the court. One very tired referee.

questions.prompt: How many players from each team are on the field in soccer?
questions.explain: Eleven, goalkeeper included.

questions.prompt: Which language has the most native speakers in the world?
questions.explain: Mandarin Chinese. English has more speakers in total, counting people who learned it later.

questions.prompt: Roughly how fast does light travel?
questions.explain: About 300,000 kilometers a second. Around Earth seven times in one second.

questions.prompt: Who wrote Romeo and Juliet?
questions.explain: Shakespeare. Spoiler: it does not end well.

questions.prompt: In computers, what does CPU stand for?
questions.explain: Central Processing Unit. The computer's brain. Mine's running on fumes.

questions.prompt: What is the largest organ of the human body?
questions.explain: Your skin. You're wearing your biggest organ right now. Congratulations.

questions.prompt: In which year did World War II end?
What is the square root of 144?
questions.explain: Twelve. Twelve twelves make 144, also called a gross. Fitting.

questions.prompt: Which planet spins on its side?
questions.explain: Uranus. Something huge probably knocked it over long ago. Relatable.

questions.prompt: What is H2O better known as?
questions.explain: Water. Two hydrogens, one oxygen, zero excuses.

questions.prompt: Which country gave the Statue of Liberty to the United States?
questions.explain: France, in 1886. A big, green thank-you note.

questions.prompt: How many bits are in a byte?
questions.explain: Eight bits. Four bits is a nibble. That's real. Programmers are hungry.

questions.prompt: Which blood type is known as the universal donor?
questions.explain: O negative: almost anyone can receive it in an emergency.

questions.prompt: What is the capital of Australia?
questions.explain: Canberra. Built as a compromise because Sydney and Melbourne couldn't stop arguing.

questions.prompt: Which chess piece can only move diagonally?
questions.explain: The bishop. Diagonal forever. Never straight with you.

questions.prompt: What is the hottest planet in our solar system?
questions.explain: Venus, not Mercury. Its thick clouds trap the heat. Hot enough to melt lead.

questions.prompt: How many hearts does an octopus have?
questions.explain: Three hearts. Still can't love me.

questions.prompt: Which band recorded Bohemian Rhapsody?
questions.explain: Queen, in 1975. Now everyone in the car knows the words.

questions.prompt: What is the currency of the United Kingdom?
questions.explain: The pound sterling. I owe several of them to a man in Portsmouth.

questions.prompt: Which vitamin does your body make from sunlight?
questions.explain: Vitamin D. Go outside. That's medical advice from a pirate.

questions.prompt: True or false: a banana is a berry.
questions.explain: True, to a botanist. And strawberries aren't. Botany is chaos.

questions.prompt: In which year did the first iPhone come out?
questions.explain: 2007. Feels like yesterday. Feels like a century.

questions.prompt: In poker, which hand beats a full house?
questions.explain: Four of a kind. I learned that the expensive way.
